saints.name: St. Richard of Chichester
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The devoted Bishop of Chichester whose prayer still asks to know, love, and follow Christ more nearly…
biography: Born about 1197 near Droitwich and orphaned young, Richard de Wych laboured on his brother's farm to restore the impoverished family estate, then gave it up for study at Oxford, Paris, and Bologna. Returning to England, he became chancellor of Oxford and, in 1237, chancellor of Canterbury under Edmund of Abingdon, whose exile at Pontigny he shared.

Elected bishop of Chichester in 1244, he was opposed by Henry III, who seized the see's revenues; Innocent IV consecrated him at Lyons in 1245, but for two years Richard lived on charity, lodging with a parish priest at Tarring and visiting his diocese on foot. Restored, he reformed his clergy by exact statutes and gave himself to almsgiving and personal austerity.

He died at the Maison Dieu in Dover on 3 April 1253, sent to preach a crusade, and was canonized by Urban IV in 1262; his shrine at Chichester drew pilgrims until Henry VIII destroyed it in 1538. The deathbed prayer ascribed to him — to know Christ more clearly, love him more dearly, follow him more nearly — is still beloved, and he is patron of his own diocese.
saints.knownFor: His pastoral holiness and the prayer that bears his name.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 3 April
